pamphlet_excerpts: Hazards, First Aid & Safety: Water is essential for nearly every bodily function (p. 48).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 2: People wholose more water than they take in risk becoming dehydrated (p. 48).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 3: The first sign of dehydration usually is dark urine (p. 48).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 4: Other signs can include weariness, headache, body aches, and confusion (p. 48).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Heat exhaustion, heatstroke, and hypothermia might all becaused in part by dehydration (p. 48).
Step 2 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Prevent dehydration and heat reactions by drinking plenty of fluids (p. 48).
Step 3 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): That is easy to do on hot summer days when you arethirsty (p. 48).
Step 4 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): It is just as important in cold weather when you mightnot feel thirsty (p. 48).

Leave No Trace and Outdoor Ethics Principle 2: Leave No Trace is just one set of principles that canhelp you live up to that responsibility and enjoy the outdoorsfully by knowing (p. 28).
Leave No Trace and Outdoor Ethics Principle 3: As you and your group plan a hike, ask yourselves how you can follow each of the principles of Leave No Trace (p. 28).

Leave No Trace and Outdoor Ethics Principle 4: Leave No Trace and The Outdoor Code are principles that help you respect the environment and be considerate to others who areenjoying the outdoors (p. 28).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Leave No Trace and Outdoor Ethics): Explain your desired route and askhow you can best implement Leave No Trace (p. 28).
Step 2 (Leave No Trace and Outdoor Ethics): Here are someadditional guidelines to remember (p. 28).
Step 3 (Leave No Trace and Outdoor Ethics): Remember this solid guideline: Pack it in, pack (p. 28).
Step 4 (Leave No Trace and Outdoor Ethics): Make it easier on yourself by limiting the amount of potential trash you take (p. 28).

pamphlet_excerpts: Hiking is an aerobic activity: Setting off on a hike without properly preparing can havedisastrous results (p. 33).
Hiking is an aerobic activity Principle 2: Make sure you are ready, from your physical condition to the best gear for the trip (p. 33).
Hiking is an aerobic activity Principle 3: To enjoy hiking to the fullest, you will want to be in goodshape (p. 33).
Hiking is an aerobic activity Principle 4: That is why requirement 3 calls for developing a plan for conditioning yourself (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hiking is an aerobic activity): Begin with short trips, increasing the length of your journeys as you become more fit (p. 33).
Step 2 (Hiking is an aerobic activity): A goodway to prepare for Scout hikes is to walk when­ever you canrather than riding in a car or relying on public transit (p. 33).
Step 3 (Hiking is an aerobic activity): The word aerobic means "with oxygen." Aerobic activitiesincrease the rate of your breathing and your heartbeat, andpush your body to use oxygen (p. 33).
Step 4 (Hiking is an aerobic activity): Aerobic training can strengthen your circula­tory and respiratory systems, add mass to muscles and bones, burn excess fat, and lead toimprovements (p. 33).

Prepare a written hike plan before each hike and share it with your counselor or a designee for approval before starting the hike.
